title: Article 138 — Enlargement of the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court

content.overview: Article 138 provides that the Supreme Court shall have such further jurisdiction and powers with respect to any of the matters in the Union List as Parliament may by law confer. It shall also have such further jurisdiction and powers with respect to any matter as the Government of India and the Government of any State may by special agreement confer, if Parliament by law provides for the exercise of such jurisdiction and powers by the Supreme Court.
content.glance: Parliament may enlarge SC jurisdiction on Union List matters. Special agreement (Union + State) + parliamentary law may also confer further jurisdiction.
content.study:
Article 138 enables enlargement of Supreme Court jurisdiction:
(1) By parliamentary law on Union List matters.
(2) By special agreement between the Government of India and a State Government, if Parliament by law provides for the exercise of such jurisdiction by the SC.

Examination: two pathways; Union List; special agreement + law.

sections.heading: Two pathways
sections.body:
1. Parliament by law: further jurisdiction on Union List matters.
2. Special agreement (Union + State) + parliamentary law providing for exercise of that jurisdiction by the SC.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How may the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court be enlarged under Article 138?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 138, Parliament may by law confer further jurisdiction and powers on the Supreme Court with respect to any matter in the Union List. Further jurisdiction may also be conferred by special agreement between the Government of India and the Government of any State if Parliament by law provides for the exercise of such jurisdiction and powers by the Supreme Court.

examTips: Parliamentary enlargement on Union List; special agreement + law.

keyTakeaways: Art 138: enlargement of SC jurisdiction by law or special agreement + law.
